worst_case:
RED-TEAM VERDICT — the worst realistic adoption case is an unattended overnight ultracode/fleet run, in a [cyber]-fallback account state, on the GLM/z.ai bridge plane, with the rule freshly shipped. Four disbenefit vectors, all priced against on-disk/external evidence:

(1) RESTORED DEATH-MODE BY DEFAULT — the dominant cost. Inherit-by-default + discipline #3's ban on mid-flight pins restores the estate-measured subagent death mode: 6/29 fanned-out subagents died vs 0/60 main-loop calls, and a reflex pin to claude-opus-4-8 dodged it (auto-memory reference_workflow_agent_model_pinning; reference_opus55_cyber_fallback_2026-09-25 — [cyber] trips were account/server state, 13/13 trivial prompts, recurring across days). The old fix cost ~30s; under this rule the dispatcher must ESCALATE to an owner who is asleep. Overnight: ~20% of a 60-agent run dies or halts, re-dispatch burns quota — hours of wall-clock per storm event. Frequency: highly likely 80-90% at least one such event per month of routine fleet use. The owner accepted the inherit trade in Q4 (2026-09-30), but the rule as drafted prices only the PRESENT-owner case; the ABSENT-owner case is unpriced. This alone fails the 'no disbenefits of any form' mandate as written.

(2) SILENT NO-OP PINS ON NON-ANTHROPIC PLANES — new finding this run. The official docs (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents, fetched and quoted verbatim this run) state a family alias like `opus` 'resolves to the main conversation's model... when the model family can't be determined on a non-Anthropic provider', and allowlist-blocked values 'fall back to the inherited model'. This estate routinely runs the GLM plane (this session is glm-5.3[1m]). The floor guard executed with an alias there silently no-ops to inherited GLM while the dispatch log records a 'pin' — false confidence, invisible quality loss on substantive children. Likely 55-80% to bite within the first month. The draft's layer-drift note (full IDs vs aliases) half-covers this but never plane-scopes it.

(3) MANUFACTURED UNVERIFIED FLOOD. Discipline #4 marks every unstamped result UNVERIFIED(model-axis); no native Task result object carries the served model, so literal compliance marks EVERYTHING UNVERIFIED forever. Interacting gears, all on-disk: fan-out-contract.md §A1 (measured: honesty instrumentation does NOT spill over — 'Zero inheritance from AGENTS.md §7 was measured', so the marking only happens if re-injected per spawn prompt = +tokens/spawn, or doesn't happen at all); fan-out-contract.md §A3 (measured: UNVERIFIED tags already misplace 40% under volume); ~/AGENTS.md Verification doctrine (fail-closed — 'a budget-aborted gate is never green', agent-claimed entries re-verified before building on them) + AGENTS-RUNTIME §1c nothing-abandoned → un-closable 'verify served model' items land in OPEN-LOOPS.md with no observable to close them, feeding the gap-check Stop hook on later turns. Either branch is a disbenefit: compliance = systematic re-verification tax on every fan-in, or non-compliance = discipline rot (the measured 'calibrated-silence suppressed the router' shape, 2026-07-04). The kicker: the fix ships in the box — '/tasks' 'names the model on the subagent's row' (v2.1.242+, same doc) — and the draft never cites it. A rule mandating an unverifiable marking while a native verifier exists is a self-inflicted wound.

(4) ALWAYS-ON TOKEN CREEP AGAINST AN OPEN MEASURED VIOLATION. Shipping leg 3 is a §12 row in AGENTS-RUNTIME.md, @-imported into every session (C:\\Users\\Prekzursil\\.agents\\CLAUDE.md imports AGENTS-RUNTIME.md). context-reduction.md:25 carries a measured OPEN violation ('Current violation: ~14.7k always-on tokens; AGENTS-RUNTIME.md 273L — see OPEN-LOOPS thin-docs diet') and an explicit mandate: 'A new rule must replace bulk, not add.' The draft adds ~4KB + a table row and removes nothing. Marginal latency ~0 ms (no new hook — advisory only; gap-check and git-hygiene are inject-never-block per AGENTS-RUNTIME §1c/§6, so NO false-positive mechanical blocks are possible — the block-shaped disbenefit is agent-level over-compliance only: refusing valid pins for a missing recorded owner-authorization date, or blocking mid-flight rescue pins).
